name: Magnesium before bed

lead: Taking magnesium in the evening is a common habit in lifting and self-improvement communities. Users describe deeper sleep and fewer night-time leg cramps, and better sleep feeds recovery, training and how rested someone looks.

Magnesium is an essential mineral involved in muscle function, and low intake is associated with muscle spasms. The general literature on magnesium and sleep is limited; community reports are anecdotal.

paras: Users typically take a supplement in the evening, often as magnesium glycinate, which is described as better tolerated than other forms, sometimes alongside other sleep aids. Effects reported by users range from none to noticeable within days.

The most common side effect of excess oral magnesium is diarrhea. Healthy kidneys excrete excess efficiently, while kidney impairment is the usual cause of high blood magnesium. The US tolerable upper intake for supplemental magnesium is 350 mg per day. Some users on forums report it disturbed rather than helped their sleep.

angle.text: Users take magnesium to improve sleep quality and reduce night cramps. Better sleep supports training, recovery and a rested appearance.

lead: 'Magnesium before bed' refers to taking a magnesium supplement in the evening, usually to help sleep and reduce muscle cramps. For people working on their physique and appearance, the chain is sleep and recovery, then more consistent training and better-rested appearance.

Magnesium is an essential mineral; US adult recommended intakes are roughly 400 to 420 mg a day for men and 310 to 320 mg for women, with good food sources including pumpkin seeds, almonds and spinach [1]. Low magnesium is associated with muscle spasms and insomnia, though pure dietary deficiency is thought to be uncommon [1].

Among the forms on sale, glycinate (an amino acid chelate) is described as much better tolerated than oxide or hydroxide salts, which absorb erratically [1]. Interest in magnesium for sleep is long-standing: a 1954 French paper described a 'magnesium sleep' attempting artificial hibernation with magnesium and insulin [2].

sections.h: Use in lifting and recovery communities
paras: On T Nation forums, a user reported that starting magnesium before bed ended nightly leg cramps and that sleep became very deep [3]. Another recommended magnesium glycinate 30 minutes before bed for insomnia that began on testosterone replacement [4], and others list it as part of a pre-bed stack with other sleep aids [5]. A different user reported that stopping magnesium before bed improved his sleep problems [6].

Magnesium is absorbed at about 30 to 40 percent from soluble salts; glycinate chelates are described as better tolerated [1]. Excess oral magnesium commonly causes diarrhea, oral toxicity in adults with normal kidneys is very rare, and high blood magnesium is usually due to loss of kidney function [1]. Infants should not receive magnesium supplements except under a physician's care [1].
No studies found specific to this practice among lifters. A 1954 paper on a magnesium-induced 'sleep' is of historical interest only [2].

lore.intro: Lifting forums discuss evening magnesium mostly for sleep and cramps, with mixed personal reports [3][6].
